sourcedFrom: Smith & Wesson Metal Frame Autos Safety & Instruction Manual — 10-01-15 (2015)
cleanIntro: Smith & Wesson's own field strip for its metal-frame autoloaders — the book that names the 5906 by designation — and the cleaning it calls for. Every step carries the manual's words and the page they sit on.

steps.title: Decock, then drop the magazine
steps.action: With your finger off the trigger and outside the trigger guard and the muzzle in a safe direction, rotate the decocking lever fully down into the "safe" position, then depress the magazine release and remove the magazine.
steps.prose: Lever down first, magazine second. On a traditional double-action S&W the decocking lever is what takes the hammer out of the equation before anything else moves.
steps.quote: rotate the decocking lever fully down into the "safe" position
steps.cite: Smith & Wesson Metal Frame Autos Safety & Instruction Manual — 10-01-15 — INSPECTING YOUR PISTOL, p.13
steps.warn: ALWAYS ENSURE THAT THE FIREARM IS UNLOADED BEFORE INSPECTING, DISASSEMBLING OR ASSEMBLING.

steps.title: Draw the slide briskly back
steps.action: Grasp the serrated sides of the slide from the rear with thumb and fingers and draw it briskly fully rearward to extract any cartridge from the barrel chamber and clear it from the pistol.
steps.prose: Briskly, and without a hand over the ejection port — obstructing the port is the usual reason a live round does not leave the gun.
steps.quote: Point the muzzle in a safe direction, grasp the serrated sides of the slide from the rear with the thumb and fingers as shown in FIGURE 5, and briskly draw the slide fully rearward in order to extract any cartridge from the barrel chamber and clear it from the pistol.
steps.cite: Smith & Wesson Metal Frame Autos Safety & Instruction Manual — 10-01-15 — INSPECTING YOUR PISTOL, p.13

steps.title: Lock the slide open and look
steps.action: Let the slide move slightly forward from the rearmost position while pressing upward on the slide stop to lock it open, then check the barrel chamber, check the bore for obstructions, and examine the breech face to be sure the firing pin is not protruding.
steps.prose: The protruding-firing-pin check is not optional decoration: S&W says if it is proud of the breech face, do not load or fire the pistol — take it to a qualified gunsmith.
steps.caution: You must follow this procedure every time a firearm leaves your hand, is cleaned, handed to you or another person, transported or stored.
steps.quote: Check the barrel chamber to verify it is unloaded and check the bore visually for any obstructions
steps.cite: Smith & Wesson Metal Frame Autos Safety & Instruction Manual — 10-01-15 — INSPECTING YOUR PISTOL, p.13

steps.title: Empty the magazine too
steps.action: Hold the magazine with the bullet end of the cartridges pointing away from you and others, and press each cartridge forward and out of the magazine.
steps.prose: Forward over the feed lips. A cleared pistol beside a loaded magazine is not a cleared pistol.
steps.quote: Unload the magazine by holding it with the bullet end of the cartridge pointing away from you and pressing each cartridge forward and out of the magazine.
steps.cite: Smith & Wesson Metal Frame Autos Safety & Instruction Manual — 10-01-15 — UNLOADING, p.24

steps.title: Check this manual is the right one for your pistol
steps.action: This book covers Smith & Wesson's metal-frame autoloaders, and it names the 5906 by designation among the traditional single-action/double-action pistols with three-or-more-digit model numbers. It carves out one model in a separate manual: the Model 945.
steps.prose: Check the model number and serial number stamped on your own pistol against that. S&W gives a phone number for exactly this question rather than expecting you to guess.
steps.caution: IF YOU ARE UNCERTAIN AS TO THE CATEGORY YOUR PISTOL IS IN, PLEASE CONTACT THE SMITH & WESSON CUSTOMER SERVICE DEPARTMENT AT 800-331-0852.
steps.quote: FOR OPERATING INSTRUCTIONS FOR THE MODEL 945, PLEASE SEE THE 945 OWNER'S MANUAL.
steps.cite: Smith & Wesson Metal Frame Autos Safety & Instruction Manual — 10-01-15 — LOADING CONTINUED, p.21

steps.title: Magazine out, slide locked open, chamber verified
steps.action: Depress the magazine release button and remove the magazine, lock the slide open, and verify the chamber is empty before starting the strip.
steps.prose: S&W restates the clearing at the head of the field-strip section rather than assuming you did it. Do it again anyway.
steps.quote: Remove the magazine by depressing the magazine release button. Lock the slide open and verify that the chamber is empty.
steps.cite: Smith & Wesson Metal Frame Autos Safety & Instruction Manual — 10-01-15 — FIELD STRIPPING / DISASSEMBLY, p.26
steps.warn: WEAR SAFETY GLASSES EVERY TIME YOU ASSEMBLE OR DISASSEMBLE YOUR FIREARM.

steps.title: Align the slide stop notch
steps.action: Pull the slide backwards until the slide stop notch in the left side of the slide is aligned with the forward, rounded portion of the slide stop.
steps.prose: That alignment is the whole trick. If the slide stop will not budge, the notch is not lined up — move the slide, do not lean on the pin.
steps.quote: Pull the slide backwards until the slide stop notch in the left side of the slide is aligned with the forward, rounded portion of the slide stop as shown in FIGURE 13.
steps.cite: Smith & Wesson Metal Frame Autos Safety & Instruction Manual — 10-01-15 — FIELD STRIPPING / DISASSEMBLY, p.26

steps.title: Press the slide stop pin through and lift the stop out
steps.action: Firmly grasp the frame and slide with the left hand and press inward on the slide stop pin from the opposite side of the frame, then remove the slide stop.
steps.prose: It is pushed from the right and comes out on the left. A firm grip on frame and slide together keeps the alignment you just made.
steps.quote: Firmly grasp the frame and slide with the left hand. Press inward on the slide stop pin
steps.cite: Smith & Wesson Metal Frame Autos Safety & Instruction Manual — 10-01-15 — FIELD STRIPPING / DISASSEMBLY, p.26

steps.title: Let the slide run forward — the hammer will fall
steps.action: Allow the slide to move forward. On a traditional single-action/double-action pistol the hammer will fall as the slide moves forward.
steps.prose: Expect it. The hammer dropping here is the design working, not something going wrong, which is exactly why the chamber had to be verified twice.
steps.quote: Allow the slide to move forward. The hammer will fall as the slide moves forward
steps.cite: Smith & Wesson Metal Frame Autos Safety & Instruction Manual — 10-01-15 — FIELD STRIPPING / DISASSEMBLY, p.26

steps.title: Slide forward off the frame, spring assembly held with it
steps.action: Pull the slide forward off the frame while grasping the recoil spring assembly and the slide together.
steps.prose: One hand holds both, because the spring assembly is what wants to leave first. Let go of it and it goes across the room.
steps.quote: Pull the slide forward off the frame while grasping the recoil spring assembly and slide together as shown in FIGURE 15.
steps.cite: Smith & Wesson Metal Frame Autos Safety & Instruction Manual — 10-01-15 — FIELD STRIPPING / DISASSEMBLY, p.27
steps.warn: THE RECOIL SPRING IS UNDER PRESSURE. YOU MUST CONTROL THE SPRING AND PLUNGER TO PREVENT IT FROM FLYING OUT AND CAUSING INJURY.

steps.title: Unseat the recoil spring assembly from the barrel lug
steps.action: Compress the spring slightly and release it carefully from the small radial cut in the barrel lug.
steps.prose: Compress, then ease it out of the cut. The radial cut is a shallow seat — the assembly only clears it while the spring is under a little compression.
steps.caution: Keep the spring and plunger controlled and pointed away from your face.
steps.quote: Remove the recoil spring assembly by compressing the spring slightly and releasing it carefully from the small radial cut in the barrel lug
steps.cite: Smith & Wesson Metal Frame Autos Safety & Instruction Manual — 10-01-15 — FIELD STRIPPING / DISASSEMBLY, p.27

steps.title: Field strip complete — and that is the limit
steps.action: Frame, slide, barrel, recoil spring assembly and magazine. Smith & Wesson prints the bound on the same page and repeats it in the cleaning section: never disassemble beyond the field stripping process outlined in the manual.
steps.prose: The prohibition is stated twice in two different sections, which is the manufacturer being emphatic rather than repetitive.
steps.quote: FIGURE 17 shows the parts you will have after field stripping
steps.cite: Smith & Wesson Metal Frame Autos Safety & Instruction Manual — 10-01-15 — FIELD STRIPPING / DISASSEMBLY, p.27
steps.warn: NEVER DISASSEMBLE YOUR HANDGUN BEYOND THE FIELD STRIPPING PROCESS OUTLINED IN THIS MANUAL.

deepAbsentReason: Smith & Wesson bounds this book twice: "NEVER DISASSEMBLE YOUR HANDGUN BEYOND THE FIELD STRIPPING PROCESS OUTLINED IN THIS MANUAL" (p.27) and "Never disassemble your firearm beyond the instructions in the Field Stripping and Inspection sections of this manual" (p.31). The only further procedure the book publishes is MAGAZINE disassembly (p.30), which is a magazine job and is carried in the cleaning list below. So this listing has NO deep clean — the manual documents no procedure past the field strip.

cleaning.name: BORE AND CHAMBER
tasks: Remove excessive firing residue from the bore and chamber with a properly fitted brass brush dipped in gun cleaning solvent
Finish by running a dry cotton cloth patch through the bore and chamber to remove residue and solvent
Before using the firearm for the first time, wipe preservative and oil from the bore, chamber and exposed areas with a clean swab or patch

cleaning.name: EXTERIOR AND METAL PARTS
tasks: Clean the exterior of the firearm using a non-abrasive cleaning cloth
After cleaning, lightly coat the metal parts — internal and external — with a high quality gun oil
Remove any gun cleaning solution, oil and fingerprints from the outside surfaces; finger moisture left behind can start corrosion
Never use ammoniated or other strong alkaline solvents on a Smith & Wesson firearm, and avoid prolonged solvent immersion or ultrasonic cleaning

cleaning.name: LUBRICATION
tasks: Place a single drop of firearm lubricant along each rail of the frame
Apply two drops of lubricant to the barrel
Do not over-lubricate — excess lubricant collects unburned powder and carbon residue and can interfere with function
In a cold climate use an oil light enough that it will not congeal

cleaning.name: MAGAZINE (S&W'S OWN PROCEDURE)
tasks: Wear safety glasses; the magazine spring is under pressure — control the spring and follower so they cannot fly out
Using a drift punch, depress the buttplate catch through the hole in the buttplate
Slide the buttplate out of the tube while holding the buttplate catch in the tube
Remove the buttplate catch and spring out through the bottom of the tube, then turn the tube right side up and remove the follower through the bottom
Reassemble with the notched end of the follower toward the round side of the tube

cleaning.name: AFTER ADVERSE CONDITIONS AND BEFORE STORAGE
tasks: Whenever the firearm has been exposed to sand, dust, extreme humidity, water or other adverse conditions, it must be cleaned and lubricated
For extended storage, oil the bore, chambers and internal working mechanism and coat the external mechanism and barrel with an anti-rust oil
Do not store the firearm in leather or heavy cloth, and never with a plug in the barrel
Every time you clean it, check it for signs of wear — if wear is noted, do not use the firearm

reassembly: Point the rear of the slide away from you with the bottom of the slide turned up, and replace the barrel so the muzzle is flush with the end of the slide and the barrel lug is turned up, away from the ejection port.
Replace the recoil spring on the recoil spring guide and insert the spring end of the assembly into the guide housing.

Grasp the recoil spring guide bushing and pull it toward you just enough to engage it securely in the small radial machine cut in the barrel lug, centred — if it is not centred it will protrude from the slide after assembly.
Place the hammer in the forward position by pulling the trigger while slowing the hammer's motion with your thumb, and put the slide-mounted decocking lever fully up in the "fire" position.

Holding slide and recoil spring guide firmly in one hand, move the rear of the slide onto the frame rails, depressing the ejector, sear release and firing pin safety levers down into their frame slots.

Align the slide stop notch on the slide with the slide stop hole in the frame, insert the slide stop, let the slide return fully forward, and move the decocking safety lever fully down to the safe position.
fncheck: Re-run the manual's own INSPECTING YOUR PISTOL procedure (pp.13–15) before the pistol goes back into service: muzzle safe, finger off the trigger, decocking lever down, magazine out, slide drawn fully back and locked open, chamber and bore checked, and the breech face examined to confirm the firing pin is not protruding.
